items.anchor:
They sequester 
CO2 from the atmosphere and store it in their biomass
items.note: Narrative storage mechanism present; numeric stocks must not become annual removal rates. Resolve original-source lineage before staging.

items.anchor:
They cannot 
be seen as direct carbon gain
items.note: Potential mature stocks mix biomass gains and soil gains/avoided losses. VONT carbon_sequestration is a rate; no equivalent stock outcome found.

items.anchor:
0.069 GT 
of carbon in aboveground biomass
items.note: 0.069 GT biomass and 0.296 GT soil potential; historical-loss footprint, no time denominator. Household-emission equivalents are communication conversions, not restoration observations.

items.anchor: less than 50 tonnes of carbon per hectare of restoration
items.note: Country-level mature biomass model values; no establishment threshold or annual sequestration rate.

items.anchor: Map 4.1: Soil Carbon.
items.note: Maps 4.1/4.2: modelled stock geography. No raster or visual digitisation performed.

items.anchor:
rapidly 
diminish wave-energy
items.note: Narrative erosion, wave and flood mechanisms; Spalding2014 and Losada2018 referrals. Preserve separate outcomes; no local restoration magnitude inferred.

items.anchor: some 12.5 million people
items.note: Existing-cover benefit; original >18 million and $82 billion annual avoided damage differ from fitted map subset. People protected is not flood depth or economic return per hectare.

items.anchor:
it is not possible to extrapolate 
directly from these datasets to the restorable areas
items.note: Per-area averages indicative only; continuation on PDF19 permits higher or lower restoration returns.

items.anchor: it may take 10 years or more
items.note: Expert restoration timing claim: initial benefits may emerge in couple of years, dense barrier later. Not a calibrated threshold or independent measured effect.

items.anchor: Map 5.1: Coastal protection provided by existing mangroves in 2016.
items.note: Current protection distribution, not restoration response surface. No map digitisation.

items.anchor: provide a critical shelter
items.note: Nursery/shelter/food mechanism. Hutchison2014 referral is a synthesis; trace its original studies before treating claims as independent.

items.anchor:
Reliable 
data on enhancement were only available for 39 species.
items.note: 32 finfish plus seven invertebrates. Preserve listed taxa in source; pooled model output, not 39 independent studies. Table6.1 caption says40: unresolved internal conflict.

items.anchor: young-of-the-year fish recruited
items.note: Finfish recruits include non-commercial sizes; mortality may reduce counts by one or two orders of magnitude. Invertebrates include all post-settlement year classes. No equivalent recruitment-count VONT found; never proxy to income or catch.

items.anchor: no data for invertebrates beyond the Pacific coast
items.note: Americas data uneven; West Africa no invertebrate data, sparse finfish. N/A is not zero. Regional totals not directly comparable.

items.anchor:
a further 23 
trillion finfish and 40 trillion invertebrates each year
items.note: Current estimates422/594 trillion, restoration23/40 trillion. Rounded headline60 trillion differs from component sum63; retain native totals without harmonisation.

items.anchor: Map 6.1: Benefits of restoration
items.note: Modelled recruitment, not harvest. No map digitisation.

items.anchor:
over 39% of the world’s remaining mangrove 
forests fall inside protected areas
items.note: Protected-area extent, not restoration effect or universal legal exclusion.

items.anchor:
we cannot 
use these losses as a direct metric for assessing the 
effectiveness of protection
items.note: Losses begin1996; many designations later or dates missing. Preserve this continuation when interpreting PDF24–25 statistics.

items.anchor:
rates of degradation of mangroves in protected 
areas (0.57%)
items.note: 0.57% vs1.3% outside from table; association in current2016 status, not causal restoration effect. Regional reversals retained in table inventory.

items.anchor:
they secure issues of land 
ownership and create a framework for legal censure
items.note: M2b/M6 governance narrative; cannot imply every protected area is excluded from restoration. External water/sediment pressures beyond boundaries remain.
